title: Burst capacity handshake failure causing unexpected capacity evictions for hybrid tenants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers on hybrid routing (hosted -> dedicated fallback) observed sudden request failures and mass connection evictions during transient traffic spikes. Investigation shows the burst capacity "handshake" between the orchestrator and per-tenant admission controller failed to reconcile capacity tokens, leading to aggressive eviction of warm workers and subsequent 429/502 spikes across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments.
impact: High: Multiple customers experienced user-facing errors and increased latency during a 14-minute window. Affected customers include AcmeMessaging, FinRidge (dedicated), and two small private deployments. Incident resulted in escalations to SRE and Account teams and one contractual SLA credit request.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure hybrid routing for tenant X: primary hosted, fallback dedicated pool Y with burst enabled.
2) Run steady baseline of 50 rps.
3) Inject a 10s spike of 1500 rps from distinct client IPs (simulate sudden ramp).
4) Observe admission controller logs and orchestrator token exchange; note negative token calculations and abrupt worker close events.
5) Monitor tenant-level eviction metric 'tenant.worker.evictions' and global 429 rate.
mitigation_actions: 2026-02-25 18:22 — Emergency mitigation: Increased dedicated pool reserved capacity for affected tenants and temporarily disabled burst-to-fallback routing for AcmeMessaging.

2026-02-25 18:40 — Deployed hotfix to admission controller to stop immediate eviction when token reconciliation returns inconsistent state (fail-open: preserve workers until reconciliation completes). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/5270
2026-02-25 19:05 — Communication: Notified impacted customers and Account teams; created incident channel and interim postmortem draft.
2026-02-26 09:12 — Added synthetic canary that replays spike traffic to verify mitigation holds in Hosted and Dedicated environments.
root_cause: A race during the burst token exchange handshake between the orchestrator and per-tenant admission service. When orchestrator sent a 'grant-burst' token and the admission service returned a partial acknowledgment (due to a transient gRPC timeout), the orchestrator treated the response as a failure and emitted a negative credit delta. Negative deltas triggered the eviction policy which closed warm workers prematurely. The problem was exacerbated by a legacy assumption in the eviction logic: any negative delta > 0 was interpreted as sustained oversubscription rather than transient inconsistency.
proposed_solution:
1) Make the burst token handshake idempotent and tolerant: require explicit ACK with sequence number; ignore transient NACK/timeouts for up to 3s and retry at backoff.
2) Stop using negative deltas to trigger immediate evictions — add a short grace window (configurable, default 5s) before evicting warm workers.
3) Add stronger metrics and traces across handshake path (orchestrator -> admission -> proxy) and an alert if exchange latency > 200ms.
4) Backfill unit and integration tests that simulate partial ACKs and timeouts.
rollout_plan:
1) Land change in orchestrator and admission controller on internal canary (staging) with synthetic spike tests (Cycle 2026-W09).
2) Gradual rollout to Hosted control plane: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours with increased traffic replay.
3) For Dedicated customers with reserved capacity, schedule a coordinated maintenance window to apply the fix (announce 72h in advance).
4) For private/on-prem deployments, ship patch notes and provide an assisted upgrade path; offer emergency patch for high-impact customers.
qa_criteria:
- Canary passes 10k spike replay with no more than baseline evictions and 429 rate within SLA.
- Regression tests for handshake idempotency and negative-delta handling added to CI.
- Grafana dashboard shows handshake latency and a new 'eviction-grace' metric behaving as configured.
- On-call SRE confirms no regression in other admission behaviours (token exhaustion, steady-state throughput).
notes: Design review scheduled with Runtime team on 2026-03-04. Need SRE sign-off before wide rollout. Account team requested a customer-facing summary for support and a post-fix validation report for the three impacted accounts.
